title: Route beta updates through a stable channel pointer
summary: Replace the prerelease-incompatible releases/latest beta updater route with a serialized, stable, integrity-verified channel metadata pointer.
reason: Remediate AUDIT-FIND-W10-011, where GitHub's latest-release endpoint excludes prereleases, and the coupled AUDIT-FIND-W10-015 publication race that could advance mixed or competing channel state.
behavior_before: Beta clients were configured for releases/latest/download/latest-beta.json even though GitHub excludes prereleases from latest-release resolution.
behavior_after: Beta and stable clients use dedicated updater-<channel> pointer releases; serialized publication advances a pointer only after versioned assets succeed and accepts it only when the exact public endpoint returns the just-published bytes.
tests_added: New pointer publication creates a prerelease, explicitly excludes it from latest selection, targets the exact source SHA, and verifies the exact configured endpoint.
Existing pointer publication replaces only the channel JSON asset after validating tag, title, draft/prerelease, mutability, and asset-scope policy.
Mismatched channel version or installer provenance is rejected before remote access, and stale endpoint bytes fail post-publication acceptance.
Workflow policy asserts repository/channel serialization with cancellation disabled and versioned release publication before pointer advancement.
manual_validation: PowerShell and workflow YAML parsing passed; the GitHub audit-spine checker passed.
Touched Python Ruff and compileall passed; 58 private-beta/updater-pointer tooling tests passed.
Risky-file registry, test-subsystem inventory, architecture, naming, and god-file checks passed; god-file output contained warnings only.

A full Windows release build with -Zip -Verify -IncludeTests copied 18,470 files and ran for 924 seconds. Package policy, environment, Tauri prerequisites, tool integration, and end-to-end smoke passed; aggregate verification exited 1 only on established WebView static-asset, dependency-cycle, generated/status-document, tracked-office-document, and unrelated Ruff baselines.

A fresh -IncludeTests release-policy copy contained 18,470 files; 22 included implementation, test, documentation, and generated paths matched the source tree by SHA-256, and focused packaged tests passed 9 tests with 3 expected skips for workflow/change-control metadata intentionally omitted from deployable packages.

Not run locally: Rung 6 isolated GitHub repository publication, exact real HTTP endpoint retrieval, updater client canary, simultaneous dispatch serialization, forced interruption, and retry/coherence validation. This external prerequisite keeps the packet in_progress.
rollback_plan: Revert the channel-pointer publication, endpoint generation and verification, focused tests, documentation, generated artifacts, and packet metadata together.
notes: High-risk release/updater boundary. Local tests use disposable fake GitHub and endpoint-fetcher scripts only. No GitHub mutation, release publication, signing, lifecycle action, media access, or source-media mutation occurred. Disposable release candidates under C:\Users\lmmye\AppData\Local\Temp\mediapipeline-updater-pointer-039-* were manifest-checked and removed after validation. Existing dirty worktree changes belong to prior bounded audit batches and were preserved. Immutable audit evidence remained read-only.
